If we plug in $x=1$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so  we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x+1}{({x}^{2}-9)^{2}+32x-96} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{[{x}^{2}-2x+1]}^{′}}{{[({x}^{2}-9)^{2}+32x-96]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{2x-2}{4x({x}^{2}-9)+32} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{x-1}{2{x}^{3}-18x+16}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x+1}{({x}^{2}-9)^{2}+32x-96} & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{x-1}{2{x}^{3}-18x+16} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{{[x-1]}^{′}}{{[2{x}^{3}-18x+16]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{1}{6{x}^{2}-18} \\  & =\frac{1}{6(1)^{2}-18} \\  & =-\frac{1}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
